title: むしろ — rather, if anything
summary: An adverb that compares two things and says 'if anything, the latter.' It is also used when reality is the opposite of what was expected or commonly believed.

patterns.gloss: A というより むしろ B

patterns.form: AどころかむしろB／AよりむしろB
patterns.gloss: A どころか むしろ B

body.p: 彼は学者というよりむしろ芸術家だ means he could be called a scholar, but he is more an artist. 面倒どころか、むしろ楽しい states the opposite (fun) of what was expected (a bother).
A softer version of 'B is better than A,' showing the speaker's judgment that B fits more than A. A form like AくらいならむしろB also exists. A and B concern the same topic with opposing content.

examples.ja: 彼（かれ）は学者（がくしゃ）というより、むしろ芸術家（げいじゅつか）だ。
examples.romaji: Kare wa gakusha to iu yori, mushiro geijutsuka da.
examples.tr: He's not so much a scholar as rather an artist.

examples.ja: 掃除（そうじ）は面倒（めんどう）どころか、むしろ楽（たの）しい。
examples.romaji: Sōji wa mendō dokoro ka, mushiro tanoshii.
examples.tr: Cleaning isn't a bother; if anything, it's fun.

examples.ja: 安（やす）い物（もの）を買（か）うより、むしろ長（なが）く使（つか）える物（もの）を選（えら）びたい。
examples.romaji: Yasui mono o kau yori, mushiro nagaku tsukaeru mono o erabitai.
examples.tr: Rather than buying cheap things, I'd sooner choose ones that last a long time.

pitfalls: It sounds odd without something to compare with; put the comparison first.
むしろ does not mean 'more.' It is not a word that raises a degree.
